song.title: If You Could Read My Mind

guitar.notes: Folk singer-songwriter known for acoustic guitar, but no single iconic model strongly documented.

tone.summary: Acoustic simulation chain focusing on warmth, natural resonance, and fingerpicked clarity, avoiding all gain stages.
corrections: prioritize acoustic sim over clean electric

rig.name: Gordon Lightfoot - If You Could Read My Mind - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain intimacy.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for clean recordings.

blocks.purpose: Smooth dynamics and add subtle body resonance to the acoustic simulation.
blocks.gap: The Comp module is used here to mimic the gentle compression of a close studio microphone, rather than traditional guitar comp.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. No gain or drive is desired for this acoustic folk tone.
Provide a clean, warm foundation that simulates the natural resonance of an acoustic instrument without sounding like an electric amp.
blocks.gap: The US Deluxe is chosen for its classic clean circuit tone, which best approximates the 'natural body' sound required. The gain must be kept extremely low.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a close-mic studio recording environment and provide a focused, intimate sound.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is the most appropriate cabinet for simulating a small, controlled studio setting suitable for folk recordings.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the warmth and body (low-mids) while slightly rolling off harsh high frequencies to maintain a vintage, warm folk sound.
blocks.gap: Used for subtle tonal sculpting required by the genre, focusing on depth over brightness.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. No filtering or wah effect is appropriate for this delicate acoustic style.
Bypass. Modulation is generally avoided in intimate acoustic folk settings unless specifically required.
Bypass. Delay effects are explicitly avoided to maintain the dry, intimate feel.
Provide the bare minimum of natural room ambience without sounding artificial or overly wet.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly to simulate a real, small recording space, adhering to the 'subtle room' requirement.

improvements.summary: Replace the generic cabinet IR with one optimized for intimate, dry acoustic recording to enhance realism.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Close-mic Acoustic Studio IR (e.g., Neumann U47 or vintage ribbon mic)
proposals.reason: Enhance the natural, dry, and intimate sound required for folk recordings.
